A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Causal Forcing work. The main text, equations, four tables, ten figures, and Appendices A-D are readable and matchable despite repagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation evaluations, a user study, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendices C-D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark, user-study, and ablation results, including Tables 1-4 and qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: Both versions use teacher-forcing AR training, causal ODE initialization, and asymmetric DMD, with the same causal consistency-distillation extension. v3 explicitly describes the inherited Self Forcing self-rollout procedure; substituting causal CD for ODE initialization is only suggested as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same synthetic training datasets, VidProM prompts, VBench evaluation, custom 100-prompt motion set, and user-study coverage. No dataset, task, or evaluated scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1-4, including the main video-generation baselines and the appendix comparisons with PFVG, BAgger, and Resampling Forcing. The added Radial Attention citation is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix D retain the same settings, including 2K-plus-1K initialization steps, 750 DMD steps, four-step inference, evaluation metrics, and the 10-participant, 10-prompt user study. No experimental protocol revision is reported.

E4.justification: The teacher-versus-diffusion-forcing analyses, chunk-wise and frame-wise comparisons, DMD initialization ablations, consistency-distillation comparisons, and student-initialization diagnostic are retained. The new causal-CD initialization suggestion has no accompanying experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1-4 and Figures 1-10 retain the same numerical results and qualitative examples. For example, Causal Forcing's Table 1 Dynamic Degree, VisionReward, and Instruction Following scores remain 68, 6.326, and 56.

T1.justification: The substantive definitions, propositions, assumptions, and Appendix B proofs are unchanged. Adding the noisy-frame variable to Equation 8's expectation and explicitly noting omitted history conditioning clarify sampling and notation already described in v1.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the architectural-gap diagnosis, frame-level-injectivity argument, and causal ODE contribution, with identical headline performance claims. Explicitly identifying the DMD stage as Self Forcing's procedure clarifies the existing contribution without changing its scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 newly explains how DMD self-rollout on generated prefixes reduces training-inference mismatch. Section 3.4 adds the untested possibility of using causal CD to initialize DMD; existing appendix limitations and interpretations remain.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a separate direct code-repository address, whereas v1 supplied the project-page address for both project and code. Section 3.3 also explicitly documents the existing DMD self-rollout behavior; Appendix D's implementation settings are unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A and the bibliography add Li et al. (2025), Radial Attention, to the video-model literature. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds a Self Forcing recap heading, explicit Stage 1-3 labels, localized explanatory revisions, acknowledgements, and conference publication text. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The first-page layout and subsequent text placement change, and Table 2 moves from page 8 to page 9. Table 4's caption adds explicit VisionReward emphasis. The existing figures and table structures are retained without new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity through explicit stage labels and a clearer explanation of the inherited DMD self-rollout procedure. The direct repository address improves code discoverability. These are useful, limited gains in exposition and reproducibility guidance; the experimental evidence and substantive theory remain unchanged.
